The train carried us west for four days, and I never tired of the window. At first the country was crowded with farms and villages, each with its white church and its red barn; then the towns grew farther apart, and the fields larger, and at last there was only grass, miles upon miles of it, rippling in the wind like water. I had not imagined that land could be so empty or so generous. At every station, men in broad hats stood watching the train go by; they looked at us with a mixture of curiosity and indifference, and I wondered what they thought of the strangers who were coming into their country. I had no answer, and only the long rhythm of the rails.
